heard: Sunlight bending through Venus's atmosphere creates a glowing halo. We all recognize the moon cycle from crescent to full. Galileo Galilei discovered Venus mimics those same phases in 1610. At full phase, it looks like a tiny distant dot. When closer, it swells into a crescent six times larger. But its most mysterious phase happens against the sun. Astronomers saw a ring of fire during the 1761 transit. Thick clouds wrap sunlight all the way around the planet. Because even before its transit, light bends around the planet's edge.
